the human brain is able to use the current physical configuration to simulate the goal of an action and to predict the goal of an observed action, which is the same mechanism that is used to simulate the goal state of a potential action.
the brain uses the body posture as the basis to simulate actions and to predict their outcomes.

the body posture of an observer modulates the prediction of the goal state of an action, and that this modulation is implemented by a common neural mechanism for planning and perceiving action.
the body posture of an agent influences the way that an observer interprets the observed actions.

the brain is sensitive to postural congruence between the body of the actor and the body of the observer.
the brain's action planning and action perception mechanisms share a common neural substrate, which is sensitive to the body posture of both the observer and the observed agent.
the brain's predictive mechanisms for action planning and action perception are not only similar but also share a common reference frame, namely the body posture.
